World map ARTIFACTS information popup — native source grammar

Scope
  This is offline source extraction from the two configured Windows PE images.
  It is not a test, generated translation, or observation of the running game.
  popup-native-images.json records the actual files and image identities.
  Addresses below are Steam RVAs; Classic view code is Steam-0x70 and the
  shared item/HF suppliers are Steam-0x2fc0. ASM files retain native VAs.
  popup-branches/calls/literals.tsv are instruction evidence, not a claim that
  every branch of a shared supplier is reachable in this popup.

Entry and source ownership
  viewscreen_worldst::render: 1c17e0..1d3abc.
  The ARTIFACTS list hover path 1d1bd0..1d1cce fetches an artifact record and
  its parallel cached rumor at worldscreen+8428. When last_hover_artifact+8448
  changes, 1d1cad calls 1d9c30(worldscreen, artifact, artifact_rumor).
  The click/feed path 1d7b17..1d7dd4 invokes the same supplier at 1d7c3a;
  1d7c63 then checks location reachability and the same two leader pointers.
  This input path is not a second text renderer and contains no alternate
  ownership/footer captions. On success it creates a recover-artifact mission.
  The render path gates the popup on a real hovered artifact at 1d2336.

Producer 1d9c30..1da27a
  artifact_description.text+8450 is cleared.
  artifact_eac+8468, artifact_rpa_holder+8470 and artifact_fac_holder+8478
  are reset, then set from actual local claim/holder records matching
  artifact.id, with the relevant claim's remote/site owner field == -1.
  +8468 is found through local entity claims; +8470 through local HF remote
  property holdings; +8478 through their associated local family holdings.
  All three can be present in the source; the renderer decides precedence.

  1d9dad..1d9dc9:
    complete_item_description(artifact.item /* +90 */, dst,
                              true /* R8B */, true /* R9B */,
                              false /* stack arg5 */, 0 /* stack arg6 */);
  The called root is c75000..c796aa (Classic c72040..c766ea).
  This call performs no item-type filter. Its input is the persisted item
  referenced by this artifact; it does not claim that every concrete item
  class is an artifact type created by ordinary vanilla world generation.
  The producer wraps the complete document at 53 source bytes, preserving
  splitting spaces, into worldscreen.artifact_description.text. It retains
  every wrapped row, including rows beyond the first eight shown by render.
  The remaining producer resolves artifact rumor site/subregion/HF location
  into worldscreen+198/+19c for mission reachability. It generates no further
  visible description, ownership, or action text.

Body — complete document, not a screenshot sentence
  Root c75000 supplies the opening selected by item type/material/quantity:
    This is ... / These are ... / This is a stack of ... /
    This is a bundle of ... / These are N bundles of ...
  c7540b -> c65450 formats the item identity/name, materials, quantity and
  designation. The item artifact flag itself controls artifact craftsmanship
  versus ordinary quality/maker prose; the popup call does not rewrite it.
  c755f0..c7569c creates:
    All {race RAW CRAFTSMAN singular}ship is of the highest quality.
  The occupation comes from item maker race via +590, with craftsman fallback;
  it is not limited to the single English word craftsmanship.

  Reuse the complete native item-description source graph in
  ../item-description-sources.tsv and ../item-description-sources.md.
  popup-text-productions.tsv binds every recorded shared body production to
  this concrete caller, then applies its boolean/flag/mode constraints.
  The graph contains type/material/RAW-title dispatch, all improvement kinds,
  dye state and color/quality/list combinations, instrument parts, chain/rope/
  rollers/handle, hanging rings, spikes, images and historical art subjects,
  sewn images, dice face/series/range/upward-face content, writing and pages,
  cloth/thread/leather base coloration, coins and rulers/years/faces, dye
  output, stored slab inscriptions, wear, every contaminant and material
  state, source kind10 item powers, tool DESCRIPTION and stored instrument
  DESCRIPTION. Their dynamic names, histories, materials, raw definitions and
  future authored mod text cannot be enumerated as finite complete sentences.

  Keep the existing external graphs linked by that catalog: statue-art,
  statue-history, memorial-inscription, item-info-title/map-hover/corpse-title,
  item RAW names, and native stored instrument/power RAW/Lua writers.
  Those sources remain the producer boundary for artistic/history/writing
  tails; nearby strings or a list of example saves is not that grammar.

  Call-specific exclusions:
    R9B=true chooses plain source spaces rather than [R]/[B] paragraph markup.
    flags=0 disables item/HF LPAGE and numeric-ID markup sent through helpers.
    The fifth argument is supplied as false; the root body does not consume
    that stack parameter as a separate text selector in this image.
    R8B=true is propagated to the existing art formatter; it does not disable
    art or restrict the document to the opening and improvement sentence.
    c77dfd, c7809e and c78e3f gate unread/literacy messages on game mode1 and
    the active adventurer. The fortress world-map context takes the other
    edge. Shared literals about writing one has not read, being unable to
    read, and adventure read side effects are therefore not popup productions.
    Writing content, written pages, blank pages and slab inscriptions remain
    real body productions. The root's embedded c79660..c796aa selector data
    is represented as bytes in ASM and decoded by the existing catalog; it
    is not disassembled as additional instructions or visible text.

Renderer 1d2336..1d286b
  It draws a closed HOVER_RECTANGLE, then copies artifact_description.text
  and emits at most the first eight rows at 1d24e0..1d2547. The remaining
  full document is still present in its source vector. Current translation
  reads that full cache through native_world_artifact_description_lines().

  Ownership has one strict mutually exclusive chain:
    if artifact_eac(+8468):
      Claimed by your local government
    else if artifact_rpa_holder(+8470):
      Claimed by local {historical_figure_display}
    else if artifact_fac_holder(+8478):
      Claimed by local family
    else:
      no ownership line

  Person branch 1d25f3..1d2696:
    draw("Claimed by local ", justification=3, width=0); // return 1d2620
    context = default_HF_context(); // 72080, flags=0, +8/+10=null,
                                   // speaker/observer IDs=-1
    historical_figure_display(holder.HF_id /* holder+e0 */, context, 1, 1);
    draw(full_HF_display, justification=0, width=0);      // return 1d2696
  The supplier b92f10..b93927 resolves the HF ID and uses the generated name
  at HF+38 through a946e0. The second word mode1 suppresses the ordinary
  race/caste postfix for a named HF (b931f6..b93207). An unnamed HF follows
  its real a/the creature description with zombie/ghostly and transformation
  modifiers when the source state calls for them. Null HF lookup produces
  "an unknown creature" at b938d6, yielding the complete ownership sentence
  "Claimed by local an unknown creature".
  The default context excludes the shared supplier's interrogator, subject,
  Nameless, unidentified-creature, speaker pronoun and LPAGE branches. They
  are preserved in supplier ASM as source evidence, not advertised as popup
  text. Names, creature/caste RAW and transformations are dynamic leaves.

  The prefix/HF draws have no resize and no explicit width clipping.
  R8=3 is justify_cont, not a width. They advance the same native cursor on
  the same row, so capture_panel_text_card reads a combined row despite
  separately issued addst calls. A long name can extend beyond the popup's
  right frame while still inside native clipx. That case has no resize-based
  clipped caption. The implemented popup reader now recovers only from the
  two actual NativeDrawnTextRow sources: exact prefix x/y/source, HF at the
  same y and x=prefix.x+17, and all visible HF bytes agreeing with the full
  drawn source clipped to the proven card edge. The whole name then passes
  through the scoped World artifact claim grammar. This does not infer a
  source from a single word or borrow another panel's caption.
  When the same native name overwrites the popup's right edge, its visible
  physical glyphs are admitted only after every byte, foreground and background
  agrees with that complete draw. They own suppression independently of the
  full name; surviving corners, footer sides and all other edges stay required.

  Mission footer has exactly three outcomes:
    if !leader(+1c0) && !leader(+1b8):
      Cannot order mission without leader
    else if mission_location(+198,+19c) >= 0:
      Click to recover (creates new mission)
    else:
      Inaccessible mission location
  Ownership selection does not choose or suppress a footer branch.
  Each footer exits to 1c6068, so adjacent request-workers/rescue/alter-mission
  strings in the large world render function are not alternative captions of
  this artifact popup. There is no synthetic Unknown/none ownership caption.

Translation responsibility
  Body stays one complete item-description document and reuses the existing
  item description, art/history/writing, material and instrument translators.
  Ownership/mission footer belongs to scoped World artifact grammar.
  The newly identified dynamic local-person branch and its long-name source
  boundary are handled there; stock government/family/footer strings already
  have translations. Unknown HF fallback is a real native supplier branch.
  Runtime custom squad.alias is not a leaf of this popup source graph.
  No desktop interaction, new tests, simulated output, or game display
  observation was performed by this extraction task.
